instructions: Review ejc3/aws, the Terraform for one AWS account. Every inline comment blocks merge until someone resolves it, and nothing plans or applies before merge, so report a defect only when you can name its concrete failure: the plan action, the AWS API error, which principal gains which access, or which boot step stops. .greptile/rules.md and the files in .greptile/files.json carry the rest of the context.

rules.rule: Flag any change that gives a dev-side host or role a path to a jumpbox (aws_instance.jumpbox, aws_instance.jumpbox_2) or to administrator credentials, by any transport. Dev side means the metal boxes (aws_iam_role.dev_server), nextjs-dev (aws_iam_role.nextjs_dev; every account there has sudo, so a role grant reaches the whole box), io-box and parallel boxes (aws_iam_role.dev_ebs_only), GitHub runners (aws_iam_role.runner), and every script those hosts run. Report when: (1) the jumpbox key reaches a dev host: `~/.ssh/fcvm-ec2` or the `fcvm-ec2-ssh-key` secret in arm, x86, nextjs, io-box, parallel-box or runner user data; a dev or runner role allowed secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on that secret; or removal of the block in local.dev_hop_setup that shreds `~/.ssh/fcvm-ec2`. (2) A key whose private half a dev host holds (tls_private_key.dev_hop in `dev-hop-ssh-key`, or `~/.ssh/runner_key` from `/dev-servers/runner-ssh-key`) is authorized on a jumpbox, or a local.dev_hop_targets entry points at a jumpbox address. (3) The administrator role leaves the jumpboxes: the aws_iam_role.jumpbox_admin trust policy widened beyond Service ec2.amazonaws.com; aws_iam_instance_profile.jumpbox_admin used by any instance or launch template other than aws_instance.jumpbox and jumpbox_2; or a dev or runner role given iam:PassRole on jumpbox-admin-role, ec2:AssociateIamInstanceProfile or ec2:ReplaceIamInstanceProfileAssociation. (4) A network path. aws_instance.jumpbox shares aws_security_group.firecracker_dev with fcvm-metal-arm, so ingress added to that group also opens the jumpbox: report a source that is a dev host (a VPC CIDR, a dev or runner security group, self = true) or a new port, and a jumpbox moved onto another dev-box security group. (5) Delegation: a forced-command key; ssm:SendCommand or ssm:StartSession for a dev role on anything other than instances tagged Role=github-runner; a grant or aws:TagKeys change that lets a dev or runner role write Role, Name, Purpose, DevEBS or BackupPipeline on an existing resource, which moves that resource into another tag-scoped grant; or a queue, table, SSM parameter or S3 prefix a dev role can write that a jumpbox, `.claude/hooks/verify-consistent.sh` or `scripts/publish-applied-status.sh` reads and acts on. (6) Code that runs with administrator credentials whenever a jumpbox plans a branch, before anyone reviews it: a new or changed data "external" program, provisioner local-exec or remote-exec, an edit to a script those run (such as `scripts/check-google-redirect.sh`), or a change to the Stop hook in `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/hooks/`. A branch pushed from a dev box is one more delegation transport. (7) s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject or s3:PutBucketPolicy for a dev or runner role on `ejc3-dev-scripts`: both jumpboxes boot by running scripts from that bucket as root. (8) Dev or runner reads that can expose administrator credentials: `ejc3-terraform-state` or its lock table, lambda:GetFunction or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, logs:GetLogEvents or logs:FilterLogEvents, ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute for userData, ec2:GetLaunchTemplateData, wildcard ssm:GetParameter*, ssm:GetCommandInvocation or ssm:ListCommandInvocations. Also report a new aws_launch_template whose user data carries a secret: dev_server and nextjs_dev already hold ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions on `*`. (9) A jumpbox enrolled in `dev-selfupdate.tf` or any other unattended fetch-and-run-as-root service. (10) Docs or comments that offer one transport (SSM, a queue, a forced command) as the safe replacement for another. Do not flag: the jumpbox-to-dev direction, including admin-box user data that restores `fcvm-ec2` on the jumpboxes, aws_key_pair.parallel_box (the fcvm-ec2 public key, which lets the jumpbox log in to parallel and io boxes), and the jumpbox publishing `/infra/applied-status` for dev roles to read; AdministratorAccess on aws_iam_role.jumpbox_admin as used by aws_instance.jumpbox and jumpbox_2; dev-to-dev hops with the dev-hop key; SSMSendCommandToRunners on dev_server, scoped by ssm:resourceTag/Role = github-runner, and SSMSendCommandDocument, which names only the AWS-RunShellScript document; dev_server and nextjs_dev launching parallel boxes through the tag-scoped parallel_box_control policy, including the ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions in DescribeForPbox while aws_launch_template.parallel_box carries no secret; s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on `ejc3-dev-scripts` (S3ReadDevScripts, ReadOwnSetupScript); the metadata-only reads in `applied-status.tf` (cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms, backup:ListBackupJobs and ListCopyJobs, dynamodb:DescribeTable, events:DescribeRule); public SSH and Eternal Terminal ingress on nextjs-dev and jumpbox-2, an operator requirement recorded at the top of `security-monitoring.tf`; and full passwordless sudo for the kids' accounts.

Flag an added or changed IAM Allow that grants more than the calling code needs, and name the narrower shape this repo already uses. Report when: (1) Resource `*` or a wildcard ARN (instance/*, volume/*, network-interface/*, image/*, snapshot/*, parameter/*, secret:*) is used for an action that supports resource-level permissions with no narrowing condition, where an exact ARN, a local list of ARNs or a tag is available. Narrowing conditions are aws:ResourceTag, ec2:ResourceTag or ssm:resourceTag on existing resources; aws:RequestTag on created resources; ec2:CreateAction on ec2:CreateTags; and a pinned ec2:Owner on image/*. (2) An action with no resource-level scope (ec2:Describe* and similar) is newly allowed on `*` without an aws:RequestedRegion condition while the calling code uses a single-region client. (3) iam:PassRole has a Resource other than one role ARN or lacks an iam:PassedToService condition, or a companion Deny on iam:PassRole is removed (DenyPassingOtherRoles, DenyPassingRunnerRoleOutsideEC2, NeverPassAnotherRole). (4) ec2:RunInstances sits in one statement that mixes created resources (instance, volume, network-interface) with referenced ones (image, subnet, security-group, key-pair, launch-template): an aws:RequestTag condition on the referenced ARNs denies the AMI, and wildcards on them allow any AMI or subnet. Also report a RequestTag value the launch template does not set on all three created types; a root volume tagged parallel-box-root against a condition that allows parallel-box fails for every instance type and looks like a spot capacity drought. (5) ec2:CreateTags that can retag an existing resource into another tag-scoped grant: no ec2:CreateAction condition and no ForAllValues:StringEquals aws:TagKeys limit, or a TagKeys list that gains a key some policy authorizes on (Role, Name, Purpose, DevEBS, BackupPipeline). (6) Any explicit Deny is deleted or narrowed, including the Deny `*` policies github_actions_terraform, github_actions_staging_retired and retired_legacy_dev_server; the Deny on ec2:RunInstances, ec2:AttachVolume and iam:PassRole in detached-encrypted-ebs-only; DenyNonLeaseTagChangesOutsideLaunch, which stops the runner controller tagging a dev or admin host Role=github-runner and so opening dev-box ssm:SendCommand to it; and NeverChangeIdentityOrReadReusableCredentials, NeverDelegateOrReadReusableCredentials, NeverReadAccountWideCommandOutput, DenyReusableParameterPayloads, DenyBulkAndHistoricalParameterPayloads, DenyOtherBootstrapCredentials, NoAlternativeDeletionOrRetentionBypass, NoSnapshotDeletionOutsideBackup and KeepVPNPrivateKeysOffDevelopmentAndCIHosts. (7) A prevent_destroy volume becomes deletable, for example by tagging aws_ebs_volume.parallel_work DevEBS=true, which DeleteDevVolumes in `dev-ebs.tf` allows ec2:DeleteVolume on. (8) aws_iam_role_policy.nextjs_dev or local.dev_ebs_policy gains an action, resource or secret ARN, or loses or relaxes a condition. Do not flag: Deny statements on `*`; statements that already use the shapes in (1) and (5), such as LaunchApprovedRunnerImages, LaunchTaggedRunnerInstance, LaunchTaggedRunnerENI, LaunchEncryptedRunnerVolume, TagOnlyDuringRunnerLaunch, UpdateRunnerLeaseOnly (lease keys only) and ReapExistingTemporaryAMIBuilder in `runner-autoscale.tf`, ReportBuildStatus, LaunchUbuntuImage, LaunchBuilderInstance, LaunchEncryptedBuilderVolume, LaunchTaggedBuilderInterface, TagAtLaunch, CreateTaggedRunnerImage and TagCreatedImage in `github-ami-builder.tf`, and RunTaggedParallelBoxOnly and TagAtLaunchOnly in `parallel-box-launch.tf`; unscopable reads that already carry aws:RequestedRegion or whose callers use several regions; actions AWS cannot scope, such as ses:SendEmail, cloudwatch:PutMetricData and the SSM agent actions in `ssm-managed-instance.tf`; KMS key-policy statements, where Resource `*` means the key itself; account-ID interpolation inside ARNs; and suggestions to narrow what aws_iam_role_policy.nextjs_dev and local.dev_ebs_policy grant today, which AGENTS.md records as deliberate.

Flag a secret value (a GitHub PAT, a runner registration token, an SSH private key such as fcvm-ec2, dev-hop-ssh-key or /dev-servers/runner-ssh-key, Cloudflare tunnel credentials or API tokens, the Mac VNC password in /mac-dev/vnc-password, an Access service-token secret) that: (1) is captured or expanded while bash xtrace is on in a Terraform-rendered script: `VAR=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value ...)`, `VAR=$(aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption ...)`, printf or echo of that variable, or the variable inside a heredoc, after `set -euxo pipefail` or `set -uxo pipefail` with no `set +x` earlier in the same bash process. That covers local.arm_user_data, x86_user_data, nextjs_user_data, jumpbox_2_user_data and runner_user_data, and every local they interpolate into that process, such as shell_setup and dev_hop_setup. A `sudo -u ubuntu bash << 'X'` block is a separate process: judge it by its own set line. xtrace writes `+ VAR='<value>'` into the boot output, and on the metal boxes dev-selfupdate appends each re-run's output to /var/log/dev-selfupdate.log. (2) is interpolated into user_data or user_data_base64, an aws_s3_object setup script, a Lambda environment block, a String-type aws_ssm_parameter, a non-sensitive output, or a print or log line in a Lambda heredoc or scripts/*.py. (3) is added to /infra/applied-status or another published status; scripts/publish-applied-status.sh may publish addresses, actions and plan state, never attribute values. Also flag deleting an existing `set +x` guard or moving a secret read above it. Do not flag: fetches redirected straight into a file with no shell variable, such as `--output text > ~/.ssh/runner_key` or `> /etc/cloudflared/creds-cc-games.dev.json` (xtrace shows the command, not the output); reads in a bash process started without -x, or after `set +x`; the git credential helper in local.claude_sync_git_credential_script, which reads the PAT inside single quotes only when git calls it; scripts that never enable xtrace, such as the mac-dev.tf MACINIT user data and the ndev-zone and ndev-rebuild helpers written with `cat > ... <<'X'`; values wrapped in sensitive(); secret and parameter names and ARNs; and the identifiers `.greptile/rules.md` lists as published on purpose. Committed literal credentials belong to aws-no-committed-credentials.

Flag literal credential material added to any file, including Markdown, `browser-manager/`, `.github/` and test fixtures: a private key block (`-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----` or an OpenSSH private key), a GitHub token (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghs_`, `github_pat_`) or runner registration token, an AWS secret access key or session token, a Cloudflare API, account (`cfat_`) or tunnel token, tunnel credentials JSON with a TunnelSecret, an Access service-token client secret, or a real password. Also flag a committed `*.tfstate`, `*.tfplan`, `terraform.tfvars` or `.env` file, and a removed `.gitignore` entry for `.terraform/`, `*.tfstate`, `*.tfstate.*`, `terraform.tfvars`, `*.tfplan` or `.env`. Do not flag: shell placeholders and runtime reads in examples (`$M`, `<ACCOUNT_ID>`, `$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value ...)`); the identifiers `.greptile/rules.md` lists as published on purpose, including account IDs, Elastic IPs, hostnames, SSH public keys, pinned digests, Cloudflare permission-group IDs, and the names and ARNs of secrets and parameters; and test fixtures such as `ghp_test` and `111111111111`.

Flag a diff that can make an unrelated terraform apply replace, roll back, taint or destroy a long-lived box, an address or key the fleet depends on, or a protected resource, and state the plan action it causes. Report when: (1) an entry is removed from lifecycle ignore_changes on aws_instance.firecracker_dev, x86_dev, jumpbox, jumpbox_2, nextjs_dev or io_box (for example ami, user_data or user_data_base64; instance_type on jumpbox; metadata_options or root_block_device[0].encrypted and kms_key_id on firecracker_dev; associate_public_ip_address on io_box). (2) create_before_destroy is removed from aws_instance.firecracker_dev, aws_network_interface.firecracker_dev or aws_security_group.firecracker_dev, or from the SSM policy attachments dev_server_ssm, nextjs_dev_ssm, dev_ebs_only_ssm and runner_ssm. (3) An existing prevent_destroy is removed or set false (for example aws_instance.jumpbox_2, aws_ebs_volume.jumpbox_home, parallel_work and parallel_work_2, the backup vaults and aws_kms_key.backup_dr, aws_s3_bucket_versioning.terraform_state, the security audit and config buckets and aws_cloudtrail.security, the Cloudflare Workers Builds token, repository connection and triggers), or delete_on_termination changes from false to true on the persistent roots of firecracker_dev, x86_dev, jumpbox_2 or nextjs_dev. (4) A one-shot migration variable is left with a non-empty default, such as firecracker_move_from_instance_id: every later replacement then boots from the dated image. (5) colton_games_workers_builds_enabled or colton_games_worker_urls_enabled goes back to false after their resources exist. (6) A bootstrap user_data fetches s3://ejc3-dev-scripts/... by literal path without depends_on its aws_s3_object, which races on a from-scratch apply. (7) Replacement or destroy of aws_eip.jumpbox, jumpbox_2, firecracker_dev, x86_dev or nextjs_dev. None carries prevent_destroy, the Cloudflare account token is IP-pinned to the jumpbox addresses, and AGENTS.md lists the dev EIPs as addresses to keep. (8) Replacement of tls_private_key.dev_hop or dev_to_runner: running io-box and parallel boxes install the hop public key only at boot, dev boxes fetch the private keys only when their setup runs, and runner user data embeds dev_to_runner's public half, so hops and runner SSH break silently until every box re-runs its setup. (9) A resource address change (a rename, count to for_each, a module move) without a moved block, which plans a destroy and a create. (10) A change to a replacement-forcing argument shared by long-lived boxes, such as var.firecracker_key_name (key_name on jumpbox, jumpbox_2 and nextjs_dev) or aws_subnet.subnet_a. (11) ignore_changes added to an IAM role, policy, instance profile, policy attachment or security group, or to metadata_options or iam_instance_profile on an instance: later least-privilege or network changes then never apply, and the plan shows nothing. Do not flag: disposable compute (runner instances the Lambdas launch, parallel-box instances the watchdog terminates, ami-builder-temp); clearing firecracker_move_from_instance_id so aws_ami_from_instance.firecracker_dev_move is destroyed once a backup holds the disk; an added prevent_destroy; added ami, user_data or user_data_base64 ignore_changes on the long-lived instances; create_before_destroy added to a resource that uses name_prefix or has no fixed unique name (fixed names belong to aws-apply-time-limits-validate-cannot-catch); edits to aws_s3_object setup scripts or local.*_user_data bodies for instances that ignore user_data, which converge through dev-selfupdate or a manual re-run rather than replacement; the break-glass x86 volume swap in AGENTS.md; existing bootstraps without depends_on in firecracker-dev.tf, x86-dev.tf and nextjs-dev.tf when the diff does not touch them; and `user_data = base64encode(...)`, which delivers the script (#125).

Flag workflow or GitHub OIDC changes that let CI on this public repository reach AWS, Terraform state or write tokens, or that weaken the offline checks, which are the only checks before merge. Under `.github/` (workflows ending .yml or .yaml, and composite actions), report: permissions with id-token: write or anything wider than contents: read; aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials or role-to-assume; any `secrets.` reference; terraform plan, apply, output or state commands; terraform init without -backend=false; an actions/checkout step without persist-credentials: false; pull_request_target or workflow_run triggers; a new or changed `uses:` not pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA; npm ci without --ignore-scripts; and an existing step in lambda-tests.yml or drift.yml removed, skipped with `if:`, made non-blocking with `continue-on-error: true` or `|| true`, or its pull_request trigger narrowed by paths or branches. Also report: an Allow added to the retired Deny `*` policies github_actions_terraform or github_actions_staging_retired; a CI publish grant restored in codeartifact.tf; the github_actions_ami_builder trust widened beyond StringEquals sub = repo:ejc3/fcvm:environment:runner-ami-publish (StringLike, ref:, pull_request or repo:ejc3/fcvm:* subjects); that builder role given jumpbox administration, ssm:SendCommand or credential reads; the reviewer removed, can_admins_bypass set true, or deployment_branch_policy widened in .github/runner-ami-environment.json; an assertion deleted from scripts/test-ci-security.py. Do not flag: new offline test steps in lambda-tests.yml that run python3 or bash under contents: read; SHA-pinned action bumps that keep a `# vN` comment; schedule edits, and path-filter edits outside lambda-tests.yml and drift.yml; runner-release-freshness.yml reading public release data; the runner-ami-publish trust as it stands; tag-pinned actions already in browser-manager.yml on lines the diff does not change; and workflows in ejc3/fcvm.

Flag a behaviour change to code that already has an offline harness when the same PR adds or changes no case in that harness. Harnesses: the webhook and cleanup Lambda heredocs and runner IAM in runner-autoscale.tf, runner-bootstrap.tf and runner-vpc.tf -> scripts/test-runner-lambdas.py and scripts/test-runner-iam-boundary.py; local.runner_user_data -> scripts/test-runner-userdata.sh; scripts/check-runner-iam-canary.py -> scripts/test-runner-iam-canary.py; scripts/check-runner-release-freshness.py, the runner version pin in runner-autoscale.tf and .github/workflows/runner-release-freshness.yml -> scripts/test-runner-release-freshness.py; scripts/backup-recovery.py -> scripts/test-backup-recovery.py; backup-security.tf, backup-restore-canary.tf and the backup plans and selections in dev-instance-common.tf and jumpbox.tf -> scripts/test-backup-topology.py; security-monitoring.tf, security-external-access.tf and modules/security-defaults and modules/security-region -> scripts/test-security-delivery.py; security-defaults.tf, security-regions.tf and modules/security-defaults -> scripts/test-security-defaults.py; security-defaults.tf and security-external-access.tf -> scripts/test-security-external-access.py; security-s3-account.tf -> scripts/test-s3-account-public-access.py; dolphin tunnel routing in nextjs-user-data.tf -> scripts/test-dolphin-ssh.py; the scroll-native tmux install in nextjs-user-data.tf and its row in the dev-selfupdate.tf prebuilt-binary table -> scripts/test-tmux-scroll-install.py; jumpbox2-user-data.tf and jumpbox2.tf -> scripts/test-jumpbox-native-claude.py; admin-box setup in jumpbox.tf, jumpbox2-user-data.tf and codex-remote-control.tf -> scripts/test-admin-box-setup.py; scripts/atuin-agent-hooks.py -> scripts/test-atuin-agent-hooks.py; scripts/publish-applied-status.sh -> scripts/test-publish-applied-status.sh; dev IAM and account guards in dev-instance-common.tf, dev-ebs.tf, nextjs-dev.tf, ssm-managed-instance.tf, security-account-contacts.tf, security-iam-passwords.tf, and the Access service token in cloudflare.tf -> scripts/test-dev-credential-boundary.py; CI roles in github-actions.tf, github-ami-builder.tf, dev-staging-bootstrap.tf and codeartifact.tf -> scripts/test-ci-security.py, which only drift.yml runs. Also report: a new scripts/test-* file that no step in .github/workflows/lambda-tests.yml or drift.yml runs; a harness that imports boto3 or requests, or needs AWS or GitHub credentials or network, since the workflows run with contents: read and most harnesses under python3 -S -B; renaming a marker a harness extracts by (`content = <<-EOF` with its bare EOF terminator, `runner_user_data = <<-EOF`) without updating the harness; a third `content = <<-EOF` heredoc in runner-autoscale.tf without updating the `len(sources) != 2` check in test-runner-lambdas.py; a test that copies a body instead of extracting the real heredoc; and a new guard whose tests only feed it input it accepts. Do not flag comment, log-text, docstring and formatting-only edits.

CI runs only terraform fmt -check, init -backend=false and validate; nothing plans or applies before merge. Flag values the provider accepts but the AWS API rejects at apply, and ask for the measured size or a current AWS doc link. Report: (1) an aws_ssm_parameter name that starts with aws or ssm in any case, with or without a leading slash. (2) Growth in the code lines of local.runner_user_data with no measured encoded size. /github-runner/user-data stores base64gzip(local.runner_user_data_document), the script without its whole-line comments (#137), so a whole-line comment costs nothing. The value applied from b7ef4ff measured 6,988 characters on 2026-09-13 against the Advanced-tier limit of 8,192, about 1,200 characters of headroom; earlier that day #134 and #136 took it to 8,476 and the apply failed. Also any SSM parameter value that can pass its tier's limit (Standard 4,096 characters, Advanced 8,192). (3) Lambda environment variables that push the total toward 4 KB; that limit is why the runner user data lives in SSM. (4) Instance user_data that stops being a thin bootstrap: full scripts belong in an aws_s3_object because EC2 user data is limited to 16 KB. (5) An attribute AWS refuses to modify on a spot instance after launch, such as instance_initiated_shutdown_behavior: the create fails after RunInstances and leaves the new instance tainted. (6) Growth in the inline policies of aws_iam_role.dev_server or nextjs_dev with no measured aggregate. IAM limits one role's inline policies to 10,240 characters combined, not counting whitespace, and dev-server-role was 8,679 in a 2026-09-13 state snapshot; a managed policy is limited to 6,144. (7) Replacing an aws_secretsmanager_secret that keeps its name while recovery_window_in_days is above 0: the old secret still holds the name during its recovery window, so the create fails. (8) create_before_destroy on a resource with a fixed unique name (a security group or launch template `name`, an IAM role, policy or instance profile name, a secret name): every later replacement fails with a duplicate-name error, where name_prefix would not. Do not flag: a size the diff measures or asserts in a harness that computes it from the real source, such as the length of base64gzip(local.runner_user_data_document); comment figures are not measurements; scripts published as aws_s3_object; small Standard-tier parameters; and any claim that an AWS or EventBridge operator or feature is unsupported unless you can cite current AWS documentation.

Flag defects in shell that Terraform renders from heredocs and that runs unattended as root, at first boot or when dev-selfupdate re-applies a changed script, where nobody sees a failure until a box is broken. Report: (1) under set -e, a command that legitimately exits non-zero on a healthy box with no `|| true`, `if` or `|| echo WARNING` guard (grep with no match, apt-get update or upgrade against a stale mirror, an optional download, systemctl is-active), which aborts every later section. (2) A heredoc rendered as a script whose body ends up indented, so the shebang is not at column 0 and the kernel runs /bin/sh (`set -o pipefail` then dies with Illegal option), or an indented inner terminator that never closes; Terraform's `<<-` strips only the common indent, so one column-0 line turns the strip off. (3) A Terraform interpolation that validates but was not intended: a valid reference such as `${local.name}` or `${var.name}` inside bash text meant to stay literal, or `$${` where Terraform interpolation was meant. terraform validate already rejects an unescaped bash `${VAR}` or `${VAR:-default}`, so do not report those. (4) A re-run that appends duplicates (authorized_keys lines, ~/.ssh/config Host blocks or Include lines, rsyslog or sysctl lines, agent hook configs) instead of checking with `grep -qxF` or rewriting a whole replaceable file, or `sed -i '1i'` on a file that may be empty. (5) A re-run that restarts or replaces what the operator is connected through or a shared session host: etserver, sshd, `netplan apply` outside first boot, or the aggregate fcvm-claude-rc service. (6) A version or health check that trusts the exit status when the binary prints its version and then exits non-zero. (7) Running a fetched script after only `bash -n`, which passes on an empty file, with no non-empty check. Do not flag: failures meant to abort (a checksum mismatch, a missing registration credential, the runner IPv6 readiness gate that prints FATAL and exits 1); scripts deliberately run without -e (nextjs_user_data and jumpbox_2_user_data use `set -uxo pipefail` and log WARNING); existing `|| true` and `|| echo WARNING` fallbacks; `$${` escapes already present; helper files written with `cat > ... <<'X'` at column 0; netplan apply gated on `systemctl is-system-running` reporting initializing or starting; and `/usr/local/bin/dev-bin-update.sh` (local.bin_update) stopping, replacing and restarting etserver.service to install a new binary, with rollback when the service does not start.

Flag a change that gets ahead of the operator runbook in README.md or AGENTS.md. Report: (1) a rollout gate switched on while README.md or AGENTS.md still records its prerequisite as pending or unaccepted: local.security_posture_enabled (delivery acceptance, a usage and cost review, and owner approval), local.backup_recovery_cleanup_enabled and backup_recovery_cutover_enabled (the numbered acceptance steps in README.md), local.colton_games_workers_builds_enabled and colton_games_worker_urls_enabled (backend versioning and the ordered steps in README.md), or var.enable_mac_dev defaulting to true (AGENTS.md requires a new mac_teardown_at at least 24 hours out and a quota review). Name the prerequisite and where it is recorded. (2) A change to operator-facing helper behaviour, such as ndev, ndev-zone or ndev-rebuild hostnames, ports, worktree handling or unit names in nextjs-user-data.tf, or pbox commands and pool selection in scripts/parallel-box.sh, when the same PR leaves the README.md section that documents it unchanged. Do not flag: gates left as they are; a gate turned on in a PR that also records its prerequisite as met in README.md; internal refactors that keep the documented commands, hostnames and output; and comment-only edits.
